text: Rejects putting all 20 eligibility rules at the end-to-end level, and gives the reason in terms of cost, speed, and failure-localization rather than dogma
Assigns a specific test level to each of the five pieces rather than answering only in general terms
Puts the eligibility rules and parsing at the unit level, since both are pure functions with many branches
Puts the endpoint at the integration level, covering wiring, auth, and rate limiting rather than re-testing the rules
Keeps end-to-end coverage to a small number of critical paths, for example one happy path and one rejection path through the UI
Grounds the shape in a named model such as the Testing Trophy or the confidence-to-cost ratio
Output is structured as a test strategy with Contract or Priority Properties, a Test Plan, and Tradeoffs Accepted
Names what the recommended shape gives up, for example that unit-level rule tests will not catch a wiring mistake in the endpoint
